observations: Parcel boundary digitised from OpenStreetMap; soil, weather, NDVI and scouting values are synthetic demo data
Drip irrigation with 2 L/h emitters every 0.5 m on 1.5 m rows, which delivers about 2.5 mm per hour of operation
Last irrigation four days ago with 12 mm applied; the cycle before that was eight days ago
Soil moisture read at 20 cm; the calcareous loam is shallow, with effective rooting depth near 40 cm over a caliche layer, so the plot holds little reserve even at a comfortable reading
Leaf curling during the hottest hours that recovers fully by early evening
Fruit set is uniform, with six to seven fruits per truss across the first four trusses
Blossom-end rot on about 3% of fruit in the sandiest corner of the plot
Yellow sticky traps show fewer than five whiteflies per trap per week and no other pest activity
Grown for hanging storage as tomata de penjar, so late-season over-irrigation costs skin thickness and shelf life
